findings.evidence: Lines 340–347 only prove `⊤ ≠ ⊥` and invoke `exists_isAtom_le`; `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Irreducible.lean:148` already proves atom existence below any nonzero finite-dimensional subrepresentation, while lines 171–180 there expose the natural `[Nontrivial V] [FiniteDimensional k V]` representation-level signature.
findings.fix: State the generic theorem for any representation with `[Nontrivial V] [FiniteDimensional k V]` (preferably beside `exists_isAtom_le`), then apply it to `ρ.comp N.subtype`; alternatively use `exists_isAtom_le` directly at each call site.
findings.issue: `exists_isAtom_comp_subtype` uses irreducibility only to obtain nontriviality and unnecessarily specializes a generic finite-dimensional atom-existence fact to subgroup restrictions.

summary: The atom-existence API is unnecessarily specialized to irreducible restrictions.
